body.statement: In the instance \(\mathfrak E\), the five-edge graph obtained by omitting \(13\) has \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x_1})=5<6\) and the displayed null vector satisfies \(R_0h=(12,-3,-1)^{\mathsf T}\). Its five-atom outcome support satisfies the support-tangent assumption although eleven of sixteen joint atoms have zero probability; the signed-cell lift therefore gives a nonzero two-sided interval of observationally equivalent completions whose targets differ by \(\varepsilon(12,-3,-1)^{\mathsf T}\). Adding trial \(13\) yields two edge-disjoint spanning trees and generic ranks \(6\) at \(x_1\), \(3\) at \(x_2\), and \(9\) globally. The root contrasts are then identified although the \(x_2\) bridge is not fully recoverable because \(q_{x_2}=1<d=2\). Thus this instance lies beyond the full-rank finite-proxy guarantee of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} and beyond the single indirect-comparison topology of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}; observed-modifier transport in \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} also does not certify it because the effect modifier is latent.
body.justification: The example simultaneously tests structural outcome zeros, an explicit target-relevant null direction, heterogeneous stratum ranks, and the exact two-tree augmentation threshold.
body.gap: Published finite-proxy identification, two-trial proximal transport, and observed-modifier multitrial transport each miss at least one defining feature of this explicit law.
body.consumer: The example is a reproducible template for diagnosing when one additional comparison changes NETMOTION identification rather than merely adding sample size.
